title: Mixed Race
paragraphs: "Even from my perspective as a popular gladiator at the Zeltoble Colosseum, I don't think this is going to work."
"Um... Everyone, including Kou-san, is really motivated, but... I think we'd be better off changing our approach a little."
You said that without even knowing about Panda and Zou! If it’s an easy place like Zeltoble, even I could become popular! I’m Quay! I’m Brum Brum!
“In that case, let’s slip my ‘Drive Mode’ into the show and really make a big splash.”
“No, please spare me that.”
Father just shot that down! I’m absolutely not wrong here!

“We’ll turn this place into a fan sanctuary and use it as a base to build our popularity. With Sakura-chan—aka Filo-tan, who was a super-popular idol—and Yuki-chan, who’s just as good, people will naturally flock here!”
“Yeah, I agree with that, but… how should I put it? I think these kinds of underground idols only work because idol culture is already well-established.”
Hmm? It’s true—since this is another world, idol culture is still pretty niche here. But precisely because it’s niche, we’re in the process of building it up step by step.
“So… let’s see. Motoyasu-kun, it’s great that you’re putting on shows here every day, but could I borrow some of the Filolials who have free time? I’d like to help out, too.”
What?! Is Father going to help us out!? That’s worth a hundred men! Hehehe… Rival, it seems Father has seen potential in our side. My victory is practically a sure thing!
“Of course, that’s fine.”
“Thanks. So, all you Filolial-samas who aren’t participating in the show—”
“What’s up?”
The Filolial-samas who were here to hang out gather around with Sakura-chan at Father’s call. Hold on a second. I was planning to have Sakura-chan take the center stage, wasn’t I?

“Everyone, you can go anywhere—a tavern or whatever—and sing or collect songs as you like. But at the end, I want you to go back and tell everyone that we’re all having fun singing and dancing right here. And not just in Shieldfreeden, but all over the world.”
“Have fun at the tavern! Sing and dance anytime!”
“Wow! That sounds fun! I want to try it!”
“You might get some harsh comments sometimes, but keep at it anyway. When everyone’s having fun singing, it makes me and Motoyasu-kun happy, too.”
“Got it!”
“Well then, we’re off!”
“Have a good trip!”

Heeding Father-in-law’s request, Filolial-sama and the others set off together. Hmm, publicity, I see. Certainly, once we’ve established a base, we’ll need to get the word out. According to Father-in-law, it also serves as a way to gather intelligence or something like that. Right now, we need any information we can get on the Takt faction, which is still lying low.
“Hey, Hermelo, what did you think of Kou’s dance?”
“I thought it was great.”
“Let’s sing and dance together next time.”
“Sure, let’s hang out when you’re free from guarding the Shield Hero.”

Kou was cheerfully making plans to hang out with Zou. That’s how I was able to show off the venue I organized to Father. Slowly but surely, just as originally planned, the number of customers is increasing day by day. It seems my prediction wasn’t off the mark after all.

However… what I’m not happy about is that the merchandise modeled after Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan isn’t selling very well, while the items that closely resemble Filolial-sama—who’s been out and about—are flying off the shelves. It looks like I’ll need to secure a larger venue and put on a show featuring my new songs.
……Huh? I feel like my first Father from the other world is saying something in my head.
Is being skilled a given? Is there another element needed?

Hahaha! That’s all solved by Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan’s charm! I thought Father from the first world struck a pose similar to the one from earlier, but I’m sure it was just my imagination! That’s how smoothly the Idol business is going!
It was time for the second wave of Melromarc, and at the Queen’s request, we, as allies, swiftly resolved the threat. It’s over in a flash just with me and Filolial-sama and the others fighting.

However, in the previous loop, Takt got a little carried away and showed up. I thought there might be some kind of trap set up, but there was nothing in particular. There wasn’t even any need to trouble Father-in-law and the others.

That said, Father-in-law and the others are participating in the wave under the pretext of “cooperation.” So are our Rival forces. You, just stay in Shieldfreeden and keep an eye on the nobles’ moods. The Siltvelt wave is already approaching—it’ll be here in about half a month.
“Want to go visit Naofumimel-chan?”
“Sure, go ahead. I haven’t really been able to see Sakura-chan much lately since she’s been working as an Idol.”
“Singing is so much fun! Maybe Mel-chan should try it too?”
“I don’t think Melty-chan would actually become an Idol, though.”
“In Ofumi’s wild world, she used to perform with Filo sometimes.”
“Huh? Really?”

Father tilts his head slightly as he asks for clarification about Rival. That’s right—she did. My Finacée, that is. In fact, he was practically acting as Filo-tan’s manager. He’d play backup or sing along—apparently, it was good for “diplomatic relations.” I can play, too, you know!
“But, you know… it might be okay if we did it at Melromarc, but it’s probably impossible at Shieldfreeden right now.”
“Is that so? Well then, Sakura, I want to be an Idol here too so I can sing with Mel-chan.”
“I guess that depends on Motoyasu-kun.”
“Motoyasu, Sakura wants to be an Idol with Mel-chan.”

Guh… How am I supposed to answer this? Sakura-chan is currently an Idol paired with Yuki-chan. Breaking up the duo would be unfair to Yuki-chan. To begin with, we absolutely can’t afford to lose either Yuki-chan or Sakura-chan—they’re our main Idols.
“Motoyasu-kun, I personally think it’s a good idea.”
“What does Yuki-chan think?”
“Yuki?”
In response to my question, Yuki-chan seems a bit troubled as she rests her index finger on her cheek and thinks it over.

“It’s probably not a good idea to stray too far from our base of operations. It also depends on whether Melty-chan will accept the offer in the first place. Personally, I don’t think it’s a bad idea to give it a try.”
“Honestly, Yuki, I think you’d gain more popularity by participating in the Filolial Race than by being an idol.”
Our rival is seizing this opportunity to try and get Yuki-chan to retire from being an idol! That won’t do.
“I won’t let you have your way! Yuki-chan is a wonderful idol, after all!”
“The Filolial Race… It’s a bit unpleasant coming from a dragon, but it does have a sweet ring to it, doesn’t it? I wonder what it’s all about.”
“Oh? Are you interested in the Filolial Race?”
The panda, sensing his chance, flashes a gleam in his eyes and strides right in between them. What’s he up to?
“Lasa…”
Zou warns her in a tone of resignation.
“I do know what sort of thing it is… but it certainly sounds like something Lord Rasa would enjoy.”
Éclair replies with a sigh of her own.
“Just from the name, I can tell it’s something like a horse race where the Filolials compete.”
“Yuki’s a thoroughbred. Gaelion knows she’s an elite runner, born to race. I think she’s even better than an Idol.”
“I object to being recommended by a dragon! But I do like to run!”
“Hmm… I get why Motoyasu-kun’s favorites are Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan, though…”
“Is there a problem with that!?”

Father turned to me, deep in thought. This exchange sounds familiar. It’s the proposal for the “Eternal Filo-tan Plan” we came up with when we were trying to bring back our Rival. We haven’t made any progress, but we haven’t given up yet. Will Father come up with another brilliant idea this time?

“To take Yuki-chan’s career as an idol to the next level—I’m not sure if she qualifies as a Shieldfreeden, but—if she competes in the Filolial Race to boost her popularity, couldn’t she gain more devoted fans from among the Filolial Race audience?”
Wow! That’s definitely a viable option. As expected of Father—he always gives us such great advice.
“Gaelion, why don’t you try talking to Shieldfreeden? Since this is a project that’ll squeeze money out of those tight-fisted folks, it’s not a bad idea.”
“Rival! I won’t let you have your way!”
“If the Filolial of the Spear Hero takes first place, wouldn’t singing on the podium boost their popularity? It’s all for Naofumi’s sake, after all.”
Guh… That Rival is spouting nonsense! If he says it’s for Father, I won’t be able to refuse.
“You’re going to keep it a secret that Filolial from the Spear Hero’s stable is especially fast, right?”
Panda’s asking with eyes wide open. He’s probably planning to bet on Yuki-chan and rake in a fortune anyway.

“I think the bigger the surprise, the better. To begin with, even if people hear that the Filolial was raised by the Hero, it’s doubtful she’ll become popular right away, so wouldn’t betting on her for the first few races be a sure win?”
“I’d definitely love to see that happen. Bets where you’re guaranteed to win aren’t much fun, but it’d be nice to cash in on the first few races.”
Apparently, the thrill of gambling—and the possibility of losing—is what makes it fun. But Panda, in your case, it’s written all over your face that it’s more about the money than the fun.
“Hmm… Well, operators like that are basically putting money on the line with the conviction that the horse they’ve raised will win… So maybe it’s okay… but are you sure it’ll be all right?”
“No matter what you do, if you succeed, enemies will inevitably appear. Wild Ofumi had come to terms with that.”
“Well, I guess so…”
“Gambling… I can understand it as a pastime for the nobility, but isn’t this more like some kind of under-the-table deal?”
Éclair furrows her brow and warns Panda and Rival.
“It wouldn’t be good if we were colluding with the other runners, but we’re just doing our best.”
“Hmm… Well, maybe that’s okay then. Though it does make me a bit suspicious that the organizer already knows who’s going to win.”
“I’ll discuss that with the shadowy figures in Shieldfreeden and try to work something out.”

Rival flashes a slightly sinister smile at Yuki-chan right then. Every single one of them is so greedy—all they care about is money, money, money. You should follow the example of your kind Father and build up some virtue.
“I’ll use my organizer’s authority to impose multiple overloads and make sure you lose. Do your very best.”
“Guh… A fight’s been thrown down this far! How could Yuki not accept the challenge!　Motoyasu-sama! Yuki is entering the Filolial Race!”
“That’s right! While I’m at it, I’ll win the championship and take my idol career to the next level!”

If someone picks a fight like this, I’d be furious if I didn’t win! I’m well aware my popularity in Shieldfreeden is a bit iffy, after all. I’ll fend off Rivals’ interference, win the championship, and spark a Filolial-sama fever all over Shieldfreeden.
“Hey, Sakura and Mel-chan’s idol—”
Sakura-chan is tugging on Father’s hand to get his attention.
“She’s really stirring things up nicely here… but what do you think, Sakura? Do you want to enter the race like Yuki?”
“Hmm?”

Sakura tilts her head slightly, looking as if she isn’t all that interested. I think Filo-tan liked running too, but she certainly didn’t have the same passion as Yuki. After all, whenever Yuki-chan starts a game of tag with the Filolial-sama, she always aims to be first—even when there’s no particular reason to. Filo-tan and Sakura-chan tend to fall a little behind.
“Sakura, Yuki’s going to be busy with races, so you should just do whatever you like!”
“Got it—then I’ll ask Mel-chan about it later.”
“I don’t know if she’ll agree… but maybe she’ll let you sing as the opening act for Melromarc’s evening gala or something like that.”
“Yeah.”

And so, thanks to a suggestion from a Rival, a race was hastily organized in Shieldfreeden. The problem is that instead of standardizing the rules across all races, it turned into a combined race featuring monsters from various regions. It seems even dragons will be participating.

For the next few days, Yuki-chan trained desperately. Come to think of it, I recall that Yuki-chan’s child… had developed feelings for the parent of the body that Rival had possessed when he shifted from his chocolate form.
That must have been just Rival’s nonsense. I would never allow such a horrifying thing to happen.

That Filolial-sama…? Well, perhaps influenced by Father’s upbringing, he was quite the food lover. I remember him keeping a close eye on Rival in her chocolate body. It’s amusing to recall the memory of Rival nearly being devoured. He must still hold a grudge about that incident.

Based on advice from my trainer—and my own experience from previous loops—I made full use of the facilities to get Yuki-chan’s body in top running condition. She was more vibrant than ever before. She was practicing her running routine with even more enthusiasm than her dance choreography. That’s Yuki-chan for you.

Since there was already a racetrack in a town that looked like a knockoff of Vegas, it seems they were able to host a fairly large-scale race organized by the government. Aside from the fact that the participants aren’t all Filolial-sama, the way it’s a total knockoff through and through really gives it that Shieldfreeden vibe. I’m starting to get anxious about whether it’s really okay to let Yuki-chan participate in a race like this.

With the gloomy mood following the war, it’s said that the people of Shieldfreeden are often gathering simply for entertainment. What’s more, since the equipment comes from Takt or was already in place, the communication infrastructure is fully developed. Broadcasts can be distributed throughout Shieldfreeden, and it has evolved into a major race where people can place bets no matter where they are in the country. With guilds across the country acting as intermediaries, it felt like the race was finally about to begin.
But… something happened on the very day the race was set to start.
